facts.label: Distinct physical addresses registered for hemp retail in Texas
facts.source: Texas DSHS, Retail Hemp Registrants list dated 14 July 2026
facts.verify: Parse the xlsx; every row is ADDRESS_TYPE='PL' (physical location). 14,204 location rows resolve to 13,608 distinct (ADDRESS, CITY, ZIP) tuples.
facts.note: Use the address count, not the row count. 101 license numbers repeat the same address across rows, which inflates a naive row count.

facts.label: Unique retail hemp registration numbers
facts.source: Texas DSHS, Retail Hemp Registrants list dated 14 July 2026
facts.verify: Count distinct LICENSE_NUMBER. All 14,205 rows carry LIC_STATUS='Current'.
facts.note: A registration can cover many locations, so registrations and locations are different numbers. Never present one as the other.

facts.label: Locations held under a single registration by the largest registrant
facts.source: Texas DSHS, Retail Hemp Registrants list dated 14 July 2026
facts.verify: LICENSE_NUMBER 4071, BW GAS & CONVENIENCE RETAIL LLC, appears on 249 location rows. Second largest is SPECS FAMILY CORP at 224 (LICENSE_NUMBER 2127).
facts.note: Both are convenience and liquor chains, not specialty hemp retailers. This is the defining structural fact of Texas hemp retail.

facts.label: Retail Hemp Registration fee
facts.verify: DSHS: 'The Retail Hemp Registration has been restored to $5,000 annually per location, plus the applicable Texas Online (TOL) fee.' Requirements in 25 TAC 300.
facts.note: Per location, not per business. A 249-location registrant faces a very different cost base from a single store.

facts.label: Consumable Hemp Product licence fee
facts.verify: DSHS: 'The Consumable Hemp Product license fee has been restored to $10,000 annually per location, plus the applicable TOL fee.'

facts.label: Date the Texas schedule affecting delta-8 THC took effect
facts.verify: DSHS: 'The Texas schedule affecting delta-8 THC becomes effective July 31, 2026.' Follows Texas Supreme Court in Texas Department of State Health Services v. Sky Marketing Corp, which confirmed delta-8 THC is a controlled substance with only naturally occurring trace amounts exempt.
facts.note: LIVE RISK. This took effect 11 days before the page was written and AFTER the 14 July 2026 registrant file was published, so the registrant counts describe the market immediately before the change. DSHS states products labeled to contain delta-8, or shown to contain more than trace amounts of tetrahydrocannabinols including delta-8, may be detained and referred to law enforcement.

facts.label: Maximum delta-9 THC concentration in a consumable hemp product
facts.source: Texas Health and Safety Code 443 via DSHS
facts.verify: DSHS: 'consumable hemp products may contain delta-9 tetrahydrocannabinol at a concentration of not more than 0.3 percent on a dry weight basis.'

facts.label: Date DSHS adopted emergency 21-plus and ID rules
facts.verify: DSHS: emergency rules adopted 2 Oct 2025 prohibit sales to customers under 21 and require valid government-issued ID before purchase. Violations may result in permanent revocation. Texas Register Rules 300.701 and 300.702.

gaps: THC-A / THCA specifically: the DSHS Consumable Hemp Program page does NOT use the terms THCA, THC-A, tetrahydrocannabinolic acid, or 'total THC' anywhere. It addresses delta-8 and delta-9 by name. Do NOT publish any claim about whether THC-A may be sold in Texas. State what DSHS states, cite it, and refer operators to DSHS and their own counsel.
Post-scheduling registrant counts: the current registrant file predates the 31 July 2026 delta-8 scheduling. Re-pull after the next DSHS list to measure attrition.
Sales volume: Texas publishes no hemp sales figures comparable to state cannabis programs.
